title: restic prune fails and reports missing data
body: I am using restic 0.18.1 on Linux with a version 1 repository stored on Backblaze B2. When I run `restic prune`, it loads 422 index files and 170 snapshots, then reports many data packs not found in the index and stops with `Integrity check failed: Data seems to be missing` and `Fatal: index is not complete`. Before this, I used `repair snapshots --forget` and `rewrite --forget` on groups of snapshots because rewrite could not encode some old trees without losing information. These snapshots were originally made with restic 0.12, and I upgraded to 0.18.1 yesterday to use rewrite. I also interrupted an earlier `restic repair snapshots` run after it became silent for a long time. I expected prune to complete and report the saved space.

symptoms_visible: My prune loads the indexes and snapshots, then lists many data packs as not found in the index and exits with `Integrity check failed: Data seems to be missing` and `Fatal: index is not complete`.
N0.label: N0 prune blocked by incomplete index

symptoms_visible: My check output reports unexpected file sizes for two packfiles, errors involving missing blobs in damaged trees, and repository errors rather than `no errors were found`.
N1.label: N1 check confirms repository damage

symptoms_visible: The repair-packs command completed without an error and wrote two recovered `pack-...` files into my home directory.
N2.label: N2 damaged packs repaired

symptoms_visible: After repairing the two packs, my new check no longer reports those broken packfiles, but it still reports missing content in several trees, including tree f63d7a88.
N3.label: N3 remaining snapshot damage isolated

symptoms_visible: My `restic repair index` run processed 236 indexes, deleted one old index, and ended with `done`.
N4.label: N4 repository index rebuilt

symptoms_visible: The snapshot repair reports that missing content was removed from files under my Firefox cache, including `.cache/mozilla/firefox/.../cache2/entries/D3A15DF306F350B779C972C8D800137BB415C4F1`.
N5.label: N5 damaged snapshots repaired

symptoms_visible: Both `restic prune` and `restic check` now run cleanly; prune completed and saved about 2% of the repository space.
N_terminal.label: terminal prune and check succeed

question_patterns: Could you run `restic check --verbose=2` and share the full output?
What errors does a verbose repository check report?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the verbose check and attached the complete output. It reports unexpected file sizes for two packfiles, f3ade64cdd31ea7697ad1a9831a09d7e2f93df83f526e68c025f66d7791f3acd and 1ed8c1dd8c0f0035279b17f0b1476fab2303830857f60de55d725ed80f7404e1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: My verbose check ends with `no errors were found` and reports no unexpected pack sizes or missing blobs.
The check reports the same two unexpected pack sizes, but I ran it with default verbosity.

question_patterns: Does the check output identify any damaged trees or missing blobs?
Please include the tree and blob errors from the check output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The output contains missing-blob errors for damaged trees, including tree f63d7a881a585ff2681b0a62f991328c2e280db3a96faa42ec72eee486177cad.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are no tree or blob errors; the only failure is that the Backblaze credentials expire during the check.

question_patterns: Could you run `restic stats --mode debug` so we know the repository size and object distribution?
How large is the repository according to debug stats?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran `restic stats --mode debug` and included it with the check output. The repository is nearly 3 TiB, with roughly one million tree records and about 16 GiB of tree metadata.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c2: wplapper requested verbose check and debug stats; Silvio supplied the command output. The raw errors establish two malformed packs and damaged trees. Conclusions about age and cause remain engineer-side.

solution.intent: Repair the two packfiles specifically identified by the repository check before attempting broader index or snapshot repair.
solution.concrete_example: Run `restic repair packs` with the two full pack IDs printed by `restic check`. This extracts intact blobs, removes the damaged packs, and updates the index accordingly.

edges.comment: Issue c2, c4-c7: both helpers recommended the targeted `repair packs` command. Silvio ran it successfully; it also wrote recovered pack files into his home directory.

question_patterns: Please run another `restic check` after repairing the packs and share the remaining errors.
What does a new check report now that the two packs have been repaired?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran another `restic check`. The two broken packfile errors are gone, but the output still reports missing content in damaged trees, including f63d7a88. The output does not give another specific repair-packs command.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The new check ends with `no errors were found`; no tree or blob errors remain.
The two pack errors are gone and the same tree errors remain, but the tree errors are printed in a different order.

edges.comment: Issue c5-c8: Silvio reran check after the persistent pack repair. The repeat check verified removal of the broken packs while exposing the remaining damaged snapshot trees.

solution.intent: Rebuild the repository index from the available pack headers before repairing snapshots, so subsequent snapshot repair operates on a correct index.
solution.concrete_example: Run `restic repair index`. It reconstructs index entries from the repository's pack headers without modifying the backed-up blob contents. Do this before `repair snapshots --forget`.

edges.comment: Issue c2, c8-c10: after the broken packs were removed, Silvio ran `restic repair index`; it processed 236 indexes, deleted one old index, and completed normally.

solution.intent: Repair the damaged snapshots using the rebuilt index, forgetting the broken originals so irrecoverable missing file contents no longer block prune.
solution.concrete_example: After the index repair, run `restic repair snapshots --forget`. Let it finish even though snapshot traversal order appears random and the scan can take a long time on this repository.

edges.comment: Issue c9-c13: after rebuilding the index, Silvio ran snapshot repair. Its output identified the missing files as old Firefox cache entries and removed their missing content from repaired snapshots.

solution.intent: With packs, index, and snapshots repaired in that order, preview prune, run the real prune, and verify repository integrity with a fresh check before declaring recovery.
solution.concrete_example: First run a verbose prune dry run such as `restic prune -nvv`. If the plan is sensible, run `restic prune`, then run `restic check` and report whether both complete cleanly.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers inferred from the unexpected pack sizes, incomplete index, repository age, and historical restic version that the damage most likely originated far in the past from an incomplete index. They explicitly explained that interrupting `repair snapshots` can leave garbage data but does not damage the repository. The snapshot-repair output later grounded the remaining missing blobs in obsolete Firefox cache files.

edges.comment: Issue c4, c10-c14: maintainers attributed the damage to an old incomplete-index problem, not the interrupted repair or normal deletion of files during a current backup. After pack, index, and snapshot repair, Silvio reported that both prune and check ran cleanly and prune saved 2%.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted cause: the repository had historical incomplete-index and pack metadata damage, leaving pack entries and snapshot blobs unavailable; the remaining irrecoverable blobs were old Firefox cache content.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the verbose check and follow-up check: two packfiles had unexpected sizes, targeted pack repair removed those errors, and damaged-tree or missing-blob errors remained until index and snapshot repair.
Must preserve the safe repair order established in the thread: repair the specifically reported packs, rerun check, repair the index, then repair snapshots with `--forget` before pruning.

Must not blame the interrupted `restic repair snapshots` run or ordinary disappearance of cache files during a backup as the cause of repository corruption; maintainers stated that interruption does not damage the repository and that this damage likely occurred far in the past.
Must preview or otherwise cautiously stage prune, then have the user run both prune and a fresh repository check; resolution may only be declared after the user reports that both run cleanly.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced command-line backup user but not a restic internals expert; comfortable running exact commands and sharing logs, while needing explicit guidance about indexes, packs, trees, and repair ordering.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, detailed, and cautious. Provides command output and asks before destructive operations, openly states when technical investigation exceeds his skills, and follows step-by-step instructions patiently.
